title: Simulation of a memory-augmented program
statement: Fix a bit string $x$, a memory-augmented register program $A$ with start label $l_0$, an oracle, a Boolean multi-tape decider $D$ with initial states $q_0$, and natural-number bounds $B,W,P$. Suppose that after $N$ steps, the run of $A$ from label $l$, register values $v$, memory contents $M$, and memory-head position $p$ has halted with answer $b$, and that every configuration at time $t<N$ satisfies the memory guard: its decider calls meet the stated cleanliness and distinct-argument conditions, its register encodings have bit-length at most $W$, and its memory head has absolute position at most $P$. Then the compiled Turing machine, started from the corresponding configuration with register values zero, memory contents $M$, head position $p$, and output word $out$, halts after some number $T$ of steps with output $out$ followed by $b$, and throughout those steps every register head lies between $-1$ and $W$, every decider-work-tape head has absolute position at most $B$, and the memory head has absolute position at most $P$.
